reviewed_text: The Disability Discrimination Act 1992 covers digital goods and services. AHRC’s non-binding 2025 guidelines recommend WCAG 2.2 AA and identify AS ISO/IEC 30071.1:2022 for accessibility in organisational policy and ICT development.

The registered Disability Standards for Accessible Public Transport Amendment 2026 (PDF) references AS EN 301 549:2020 for fare systems. Commencement depends on the parliamentary disallowance period; application rules distinguish new and existing assets.

dda.passage: About document and executive summary: guidance assists organisations meeting Disability Discrimination Act 1992 duties for digital goods and services. Issued under s67(1)(k); non-binding and to be read with the Act.

guidance.passage: Chapter 3 recommends at least WCAG 2.2 AA. AS ISO/IEC 30071.1:2022 section describes accessibility strategy/policy at organisational and system-development levels. The chapter is guidance, not a separate statutory WCAG mandate.

transport.passage: Registered 2026-07-30. Section 2 commencement: day after final parliamentary disallowance day; no calendar date specified in the instrument. Schedule 25 inserts s25.2 requiring fare systems to comply with selected AS EN 301 549:2020 clauses, including hardware section 8 and software section 11 for public use. Schedule 34 s35.22 applies those changes to new conveyances/premises/infrastructure and fare-system elements installed from commencement. Other Part 35 provisions distinguish existing assets. This check does not establish the actual commencement date.

reviewed_text: Later Accessible Canada Regulations amendments introduce digital requirements from 2027-12-05 and 2028-12-05 for covered federal public and private entities, with scope and exceptions varying by requirement. They reference the Canadian standard as amended. Once applicable, new section 19.9 permits ETSI editions published more recently than the current Canadian ICT standard as an alternative.

Ontario’s AODA web rules use WCAG 2.0 AA, with exceptions, for designated public bodies and businesses/non-profits with 50 or more employees. Manitoba’s information and communication regulation uses WCAG 2.1 AA for covered web content and applications, with exceptions.
CAN-ASC-5.2.1:2026 is a voluntary accessible service delivery standard that references CAN/ASC-EN 301 549:2024 for digital platforms.

regulations.passage: SOR/2025-255 registered 2025-12-05, published 2025-12-17 under Accessible Canada Act. Amending s6 inserts ICT standard definition in s19.1 as Canadian CAN/ASC-EN 301 549 as amended. New s19.9(a) permits ETSI editions published more recently than current Canadian ICT standard; (b) also allows immediately preceding Canadian edition within three years of current edition publication. Section18 phases commencement at second/third registration anniversaries. Entity scope and exceptions differ: public entities; private employee thresholds; public-facing transport/broadcast/telecom exclusions and other qualifications. RIAS describes ambulatory incorporation, not completed Canadian adoption of future ETSI revisions.
regulations.method: web reader, amending sections6-18 and RIAS

dates.passage: Summary confirms new/updated federal public web pages from 2027-12-05, covered large/medium private web pages from 2028-12-05; mobile/document requirements for public/large private entities from 2028-12-05. Scope differs by requirement and exceptions apply. Page explicitly says summary is not legal text.

ontario.passage: Who must comply / How to comply: designated public-sector organisations and businesses/nonprofits with 50+ employees; controlled public websites and web content after 2012-01-01. WCAG 2.0 AA except 1.2.4 and 1.2.5; practicability exceptions also described. Page updated 2026-09-21.

manitoba.passage: Regulation under Accessibility for Manitobans Act requires WCAG 2.1 AA minimum for newly published web content/content needed to access goods/services and new or significantly updated web applications; exceptions apply.

manitoba-law.passage: M.R.47/2022, English provisions ss2,7,8: phased sector application; relevant web content and new/significantly updated web applications must meet/exceed WCAG2.1AA; feasibility, technology, hardship, control and product-information exceptions. Current version includes 2023 amendment. Bilingual page, English provisions used.

reviewed_text: Public-sector website and app regulations apply alongside reasonable-adjustment duties under the Equality Act 2010, or the Disability Discrimination Act 1995 in Northern Ireland. Government guidance specifies WCAG 2.2 AA and an accessibility statement, subject to exemptions.
BS ISO/IEC 30071-1:2019 provides guidance on organisational policies and ICT development.
BSI’s revision project is at approval stage, and its project page lists a publication start date of 2026-12-09. The project page does not specify the ETSI version.
